newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour slams excess profits from Eversholt sale.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour slams excess profits from Eversholt sale.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Wednesday condemned the "excessive gains" made by boardroom fat cats in the sale of train rolling stock leasing company Eversholt and other recent sell-offs.
A unit of banking giant HSBC Holdings Plc announced earlier it would buy recently-privatised Eversholt in a deal worth 726.5 million pounds ($1.18 billion).

"Today's news of the Eversholt sale, for 280 million pounds more than its original sale price, shows the continuation of privatisation excesses," shadow Transport Secretary Andrew Smith told reporters.
HSBC said its Forward Trust Group financing unit would buy Eversholt's shares for 453.4 million pounds and repay debts of 273.1 million.

Labour estimated that Eversholt's managing director Andrew Jukes stands to make about 15 million pounds while engineering director Roger Aylward and finance director Colin Habgood will both pocket 10 million pounds.
Smith said the Eversholt sale was just the latest in a line of sell-offs that netted corporate chiefs huge windfall profits.
The sale of the Porterbrook Leasing Company to transport giant Stagecoach Holdings allowed chief executive Sandy Anderson to walk off with 33 million pounds, Smith said.
The sell-off of rail operators Prism and Anglia Railways also made their directors rich men, he said.
"And there has been a near doubling in value of Railtrack since privatisation alongside a huge 700 million pounds investment backlog."
Shares in rail operator Railtrack Plc, trading at 403 pence on Wednesday, were floated at 190p when it was privatised.

The Labour Party calculated that the top 10 "fat cats" benefitting from rail privatisations had pocketed a grand total of 103 million pounds. Anderson and Jukes were numbers one and two on Labour's list.
Smith said Prime Minister John Major said nearly two years ago that lessons had been learnt from the windfall gains made by the privatised utilities.

"Today's news confirms that the government learned and did nothing. I challenge them even now to admit that they got it wrong and short-changed the public by selling cheap these national assets," Smith said. ($1=.6184 Pound)
